feedback.problem: Solve the inequality ${x}^{2}-8>0$ using the absolute value method.
feedback.worked_solution:
Bringing the constant term to the right-hand side, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-8 & >0 \\ {x}^{2} & >8.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the square root of both sides of the inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & >8 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & >\sqrt{8} \\ |x| & >2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the definition of absolute value, we must have

$$
x<-2\sqrt{2}\,\text{or}\,x>2\sqrt{2}.
$$

The solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-2\sqrt{2})\cup (2\sqrt{2},\infty ).$
